paras: The lynching of Will Robinson was the hanging of a Black man by a crowd of about 100 people at Staton's stretch, Tallahatchie County, Mississippi, on the morning of August 8, 1888. Robinson had been accused of attempting to assault a white woman, and the only report found, a Dublin dispatch printed in the Grenada Sentinel, said he confessed before he was hanged "without law or ceremony."

According to the dispatch, Robinson entered a house through a window on a Saturday night, six miles southeast of Dublin in the upper edge of Tallahatchie County on the Coahoma County line, and attempted to assault "a respectable white lady." A peddler lodging there for the night was said to have run into the room with a pistol on hearing her screams, and the intruder fled by the window, leaving a footprint.

The matter was kept quiet until the following Tuesday, when a posse of men arrested three Black men on the place and compared their tracks with the print under the window, which had been kept under a box. The posse said the print matched Robinson's foot, which had a disfigured toe on the left side. A "meeting" and "investigation" followed, at which, the dispatch said, Robinson confessed.

Because a similar case had occurred in the neighborhood some weeks earlier, the dispatch said, the people became "very much enraged." About 100 "white and colored people" assembled and took Robinson to Staton's stretch, where they hanged him at 10 o'clock in the morning.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage found.

The Grenada Sentinel printed the Dublin dispatch on its front page on August 18, ten days after the hanging, under the headline "A Ravisher Lynched" and the subhead "Short Work is Made of Him." The account, drawn from the side of the posse and crowd, presented the accusation and the confession as fact, called the assault a "hellish deed" and credited the peddler's arrival to providence. No other paper carrying the story was found.

A1 reports that about 100 people hanged Robinson 'without law or ceremony' after a posse arrested him and a meeting heard his confession to an accused assault on a white woman, which meets every part of the standard definition; the account rests on a single report.
